idiom_name: ktor-network SelectorManager (NIO selectors and selection threads) driven from coroutines
implementation_notes: On the JVM the demultiplexer is java.nio's Selector, and kotlinx.coroutines deliberately has no readiness reactor of its own: Dispatchers.IO offloads blocking calls to an elastic thread pool, which is the half-sync/half-async shape rather than a reactor. The library form is ktor-network: its SelectorManager is documented as a service that manages NIO selectors and selection threads, and select(selectable, interest) is a suspend function that resumes when the interest is selected - so the dispatch loop becomes coroutine code and the handler is the continuation after the suspension point. Write a raw selector loop only in engine-level code; for ordinary applications coroutines plus Dispatchers.IO are the substitute, with the caveat that they scale by threads rather than by readiness.
pitfalls: A blocking call on the dispatcher that runs the selection loop stalls every socket it watches; blocking work belongs on Dispatchers.IO, never on the selector's dispatcher.

Dispatchers.IO is a shared elastic pool sized for blocking calls (the larger of 64 threads or the core count), so giving the SelectorManager that dispatcher ties the reactor's liveness to unrelated blocking tasks; use a dedicated dispatcher.

java.nio's selected-key set is not thread-safe, so key handling must stay on the selection thread even though the suspend API hides the loop; mutating interest from elsewhere goes through the manager's own serialisation.
